items.title: Honeycomb-Surfels: Compact Hexagonal Primitives for Efficient Scene Rendering and Reconstruction
items.summary: Hexels are hexagonal surface elements with first-order color fields that enable compact 3D scene and image representation for efficient rendering and reconstruction.
items.whyItMatters: They reduce memory and compute costs, making advanced view synthesis viable on limited hardware.

items.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.summary: ThinkWorld shows that incorporating human video into VLA models improves chain-of-dynamics reasoning for robotic manipulation.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers care because it expands robot learning beyond limited demonstrations.

items.title: When Should We Intervene at Test Time?
items.summary: The article discusses how test-time adaptation can improve model performance on changing inputs but may harm subsequent batches, highlighting the need for selective intervention.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should know that indiscriminate adaptation can backfire, affecting deployment reliability.

items.title: Heads of Security: Learned Attention Gates Improve Prompt Injection Robustness
items.summary: Heads of Security uses learned attention gates to separate instruction and data, preventing prompt injection in large language models.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a lightweight, model-agnostic defense that boosts security for AI deployments.

items.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
items.summary: The article explores how relational data can be modeled as a lattice gauge theory, using Wilson loops to verify composed relationships and allowing independent entity frame rotations.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a novel, mathematically rigorous framework for managing complex relational data in AI systems.

items.title: KPPax: preprocess differentiable kinetic ODE for machine learning in atmospheric chemistry
items.summary: KPPax converts Kinetic PreProcessor mechanisms into differentiable, JIT‑compiled JAX code for machine‑learning use.
items.whyItMatters: It enables gradient‑based learning on atmospheric chemistry models, improving integration with modern ML workflows.

items.title: Pushing Dexterity and Safety for In-Hand Object Pose Reaching That Works Remarkably Well
items.summary: The paper presents a method for robots to reach specific object poses inside a hand, improving dexterity and safety during complex in‑hand manipulation.
items.whyItMatters: It enables safer, more precise robotic grasping, essential for advanced automation and human‑robot collaboration.

items.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
items.summary: GEPA-Curator enhances learning for self-improving agents by curating failures from LLM-driven multi-turn tasks, addressing prompt, harness, execution, and judge noise issues.
items.whyItMatters: It improves agent reliability and efficiency, crucial for developers building robust AI systems.

items.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.summary: The article explores whether large language models can autonomously discover new physical laws by detecting unexpected phenomena in a simulated world.
items.whyItMatters: It tests AI’s potential for scientific insight, a key interest for tech‑savvy researchers.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
items.summary: The paper studies how synthetic environment diversity influences training of LLM tool‑use agents for complex tasks, introducing the SynthAPI pipeline.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a systematic way to improve agent performance, crucial for building reliable AI assistants.

items.title: MuonGS: Pretraining LLMs with Relaxed Weight-Norm Control
items.summary: MuonGS studies how relaxed weight-norm control during LLM pretraining improves optimizer performance by analyzing training dynamics.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding norm control helps engineers tune training for faster, more stable language model convergence.

items.title: Multi-State Linear Attention with Generalized Second-Order Routing
items.summary: MSLA reduces self‑attention’s quadratic cost by segmenting sequences and compressing each into separate memory states for efficient long‑sequence modeling.
items.whyItMatters: It enables larger LLMs to handle longer inputs without prohibitive compute.

items.summary: Language models pretrained on web corpora collected over multiple years learn both general and domain-specific knowledge. items.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
items.summary: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria. On hidden-profile tasks both look attractive, because how widely a fact is held is confounded with whether it helps. We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates…

items.title: VideoLVR: Latent Visual Reasoning over Grounded Video Evidence
items.summary: Chain-of-thought reasoning has substantially advanced video understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, language-based reasoning traces do not provide a reliable mechanism for models to revisit relevant visual evidence, leading to visual forgetting and impairing their ability to reason over video content. items.summary: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. We compare matched same-class and different-class replacements of a queried event. items.title: MoI-Bench: A Benchmark for Image Generation and Editing on Mobile Devices
items.summary: Developing on-device image models requires considering practical user needs, task types and device resource constraints. However, existing benchmarks provide limited guidance on identifying capability gaps between on-device models and server-side models. items.title: GAS-PFN: Graph-Aware Spatiotemporal Prior-Data Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Traffic Forecasting
items.summary: Traffic forecasting requires modeling complex temporal dynamics and the spatial dependencies imposed by road topology.
